chunks: One of our companions narrated from ʿAlī ibn Shajarah, from ʿĪsā ibn Rāshid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: 'There is no believer who commits a sin but that he is given respite for seven hours; so if he seeks forgiveness from Allah, he is forgiven. Indeed, he may recall his sin after twenty years and thus seek forgiveness from Allah and he is [thereby] forgiven. But as for the disbeliever, he forgets his sin so that he may not seek forgiveness from Allah.'
ai.seo_question: How long does a believer have to seek forgiveness after committing a sin according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the psychological mechanism of divine mercy, where God grants believers a 'seventy-two-hour' window of heightened awareness to repent before the sin becomes entrenched in the heart. It contrasts this with disbelievers, whose forgetting of sin is a form of divine concealment (istidraj) that prevents them from seeking forgiveness, thereby hardening their hearts. This concept underscores the Shia emphasis on the fluidity of spiritual states and the urgency of immediate tawbah.
